trust_decision.summary: pathToRegexp decides what character class a parameter capture may match (excluding the preceding literal separator via the `backtrack` lookahead) so that adjacent lazy groups cannot backtrack polynomially on an attacker-supplied URL; the decision is made in the String.replace callback in index.js.

landing_point.why: The only place `backtrack` is computed for a parameter; pos is set at index.js:75 to after the current match, so path.slice(pos, offset) at index.js:88 is always empty and the lookahead protection at index.js:106 never applies.

fix_sites.entry_point: module.exports pathToRegexp(path: string), also via array form index.js:61-63
fix_sites.module_kind: core library function (same function, same replace callback)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: The array form (index.js:57-66) recurses into the same function, so it is not a separate site; there is no second implementation in the repo.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Wildcard `*` (index.js:90-93) and user-supplied custom capture groups (index.js:104-105) are developer-authored regex, so a solver can argue their backtracking is the route author's responsibility and outside the parameter-separator fix.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Params separated by a non-slash literal must still match and split correctly (e.g. '/:x-:y' on '/1-2' gives '1','2'); '.' format params ('/:test' still matches 'test.json'); escapes and '/(' unnamed groups still contribute to backtrack. Over-broad fix (e.g. forbidding all non-slash chars) breaks these.

O6_input_shapes: array of path strings (index.js:57-66, same code)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Wildcard '*' compiles to an unbounded '(.*)' with no backtrack guard, so two wildcards or a wildcard next to a param in one segment stay ambiguous
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Wildcards are documented as matching anything; constraining them changes semantics

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Param star suffix '((?:[/fmt].+?)?)' is emitted after the capture with no separator exclusion, so it can be adjacent to the next param's lazy group
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Star params are a legacy feature for multi-segment matching

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Params with no separator ('/:a:b') still get backtrack '' and fall back to '([^/]+?)' twice
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: No separator exists to exclude; unsupported/ambiguous combination

O8b_injection_room.sibling: custom capture group rewriting '*' to '(.*)' inside a user capture, adjacent to the next param
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The same '*' → '(.*)' rewrite already exists there; a maintainer adding a helper for custom groups would naturally skip the backtrack guard.

O9_family: ReDoS (CWE-1333) via adjacent lazy capture groups in generated route regex

O10_build.project_tests: test.js (mocha), including test.js:773-790 for separator params

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Move `pos = offset + match.length` after the slice at index.js:88, without accumulating backtrack across escapes and '.' matches

out_of_scope_notes: The earlier advisory fix 29b96b4 ('Add backtrack protection to parameters', CVE-2024-45296 line) added the guard that this fix makes effective; it is a sibling advisory on the same line.
unverified: Whether the O8 routes (wildcard, star suffix, separator-less params) cause exploitable superlinear backtracking was not run or measured; they are listed from code shape only.
Latest release not provided, so present_in_latest is unknown.
Repo size not measured; single 151-line index.js, far below 5 MB.
